one_line: Human-controlled compliance deal room where agents gather evidence without making attestations.
what_it_does: Organizes diligence materials, facts, blockers, actions, and escalation for a compliance case while constraining agent actions.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools materially improve reliable evidence gathering and enforce the human-only boundary for confirmation, freezing, and hard stops; a general UI-driving agent could attempt the workflow but with substantially more risk and friction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly describes five WebMCP verbs and says confirmed is not one of them.
About text specifies agent-readable materials, facts, blockers, and briefs while human signatures remain UI-only.
Visible product frame shows materials with provided/pending/nonexistent states and fact-ledger/action-board surfaces.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, intentional case-workbench with multiple connected compliance surfaces, but the paused media does not demonstrate ingestion, evidence attachment, recomputation, or final human sign-off end to end.
execution_evidence: Hosted demo is reported alive.
Screenshot visibly shows a deal-room materials workspace with status counts and named diligence items.
Description details six zones and live blocker recomputation.
impact_rationale: Compliance teams handling contracts, security questionnaires, DPAs, and warranties have a concrete high-stakes need for auditable evidence collection without delegating factual attestation.
impact_evidence: Narrative identifies frontier-lab vendor review and founder warranty risk as the target use case.
Visible materials include lineage, teleoperator agreements, classification, and consent evidence.
creativity_rationale: The explicit API-level safety boundary—agent gathers and proposes but cannot confirm—is a strong and memorable application of WebMCP to compliance.
creativity_evidence: Human-only confirmation and hard-stop controls are central to the concept.
Fact ledger treats each fact as a signed, sourced assertion.
usability_note: The visible tabbed workbench and status taxonomy are understandable, though the full workflow is unverified.
red_flags: No direct video/transcript evidence; embedded media is paused in the screenshot.
End-to-end evidence ingestion and signing are not visibly demonstrated.
standouts: Strong human/agent responsibility boundary.
Compliance evidence and blockers are modeled as structured shared state.
advance_reason: High WebMCP leverage and credible high-stakes use case, with a coherent visible workbench despite incomplete execution proof.

one_line: Audits WebMCP coverage across the full customer lifecycle, including reversal and exit.
what_it_does: Classifies site tools into eight lifecycle stages and flags open loops where agents can commit but cannot undo or exit.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the subject and data source of the audit, enabling structured inspection of tools, but a general agent or ordinary crawler could reproduce much of the analysis with friction.
leverage_evidence: Description says the product audits websites' WebMCP tools across eight stages.
It registers eight tools of its own for agent-driven auditing.
Visible media thumbnail shows lifecycle stages and aggregate metrics.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a coherent audit model, concrete directory-scale measurements, and a visible metrics dashboard, but the paused frame does not show an audit being run or a fix-and-rerun loop.
execution_evidence: Reported run over 475 sites and about 2,989 tools.
Screenshot visibly shows metric cards and an eight-stage dashboard concept.
About text describes audit_site and audit_tool_list plus remediation-oriented tools.
impact_rationale: Website and agent-integration builders have a real reliability gap when commitment actions lack cancellation, return, support, or exit paths; this makes that gap measurable.
impact_evidence: Narrative reports 148 sites allowing commitment and 144 without undo, and no exit tool in the directory.
Clear audience of WebMCP-enabled site builders and ecosystem maintainers.
creativity_rationale: The focus on lifecycle closure and measuring what happens after commitment is a fresh, useful reframing of WebMCP capability audits.
creativity_evidence: Eight-stage Discover-to-Exit model explicitly includes Reverse and Exit.
Project centers on the overlooked question 'Can an agent finish what it started?'
usability_note: Dashboard framing and staged coverage model appear legible; remediation interaction is not shown.
red_flags: Metrics and workflow are not independently verifiable from the paused thumbnail.
No visible before/after remediation cycle.
standouts: Strong ecosystem-level insight about irreversible agent actions.
Concrete scale claims and lifecycle taxonomy.
advance_reason: Clear problem, distinctive audit lens, and credible evidence of a functioning analysis model.

one_line: Tests web UIs through WebMCP schemas and tool calls instead of brittle selectors.
what_it_does: Loads a target site, discovers or synthesizes modelContext, generates scenarios, runs them, and checks expected UI behavior.
leverage_rationale: Structured WebMCP schemas let the tester validate contracts and execute scenarios without selector brittleness; the fallback means the product remains useful beyond WebMCP but weakens indispensability.
leverage_evidence: Pitch contrasts WebMCP tool calls with brittle selectors.
About text describes JSON Schema discovery, scenario generation, and tool execution.
Visible frame shows positive/negative wire-transfer scenarios and a Run Tests via WebMCP control.
execution_rationale: The UI communicates a complete intended test pipeline with multiple workflows and constraint cases, but no completed pass/fail report is visible in the packet evidence.
execution_evidence: Hosted demo reported alive.
Screenshot shows banking app, scenario list, Gemini/rule-based generation, and tool-run control.
Description identifies Electron embedded webview and test scenarios.
impact_rationale: Frontend teams need regression tests that survive UI redesigns and validate real input constraints; this targets a concrete testing pain point.
impact_evidence: Narrative identifies selector fragility as the problem.
Visible scenarios cover valid, malformed, missing, and boundary inputs across a banking form.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP as a contract-testing surface for browser UIs is a strong synthesis, though automated UI testing is an established category.
creativity_evidence: Fallback synthesis from HTML5 constraints creates a notable bridge for non-WebMCP sites.
Combines LLM scenario generation with structured tool execution.
usability_note: Scenario controls and target app are clear; results and diagnostics are not shown.
red_flags: No visible completed test results or regression comparison.
Gemini-generated scenarios are not independently distinguished from examples in the still.
standouts: Schema-driven testing avoids DOM-selector guessing.
Covers both native WebMCP and fallback HTML constraints.
advance_reason: Strong practical dev-tool fit and meaningful WebMCP delta, with enough UI evidence to support a central workflow claim.

one_line: Accessible-by-default browser editor pairing AI coding with live preview and WCAG auditing.
what_it_does: Provides multi-file front-end editing, live preview, accessibility auditing, design-token checks, and agent-facing controls in one tab.
leverage_rationale: Shared editor/preview/audit state can let an agent build and inspect the same artifact precisely, though a general agent could operate parts of the UI with friction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly exposes editor, preview, and WCAG audit through WebMCP.
About text describes same-tab shared state and agent-facing editor operations.
No submitted frame visibly shows the product workflow.
execution_rationale: The project description is coherent and ambitious, but the only submitted video is visibly a Rick Astley music video rather than product evidence, so execution is thinly evidenced and capped.
execution_evidence: FACTS report video title as Rick Astley official video.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows the unrelated paused YouTube thumbnail, not Blnq Studio.
Description lists substantial features but does not visually substantiate them.
impact_rationale: Frontend developers and AI-assisted builders have a real need to catch accessibility regressions while building; integrating auditing into the edit loop could provide credible value.
impact_evidence: Narrative identifies accessibility as commonly dropped in fast AI-assisted development.
Claimed workflow includes WCAG violations, plain-English fixes, and exact elements.
creativity_rationale: Combining agentic code generation with continuous accessibility and design-system checks is a fresh synthesis for a browser editor.
creativity_evidence: Accessibility audit is positioned as part of the same agent-operated editing loop.

usability_note: Claimed single-tab workflow could be coherent, but the packet does not show the actual interface.
red_flags: Submitted video title and screenshot show an unrelated music video.
No gallery images or repository; central product claims lack visual proof.
standouts: Strong accessibility-centered product thesis if implemented.
Design-system compliance integrated into AI coding is notable.
advance_reason: Potentially valuable concept, but the submission evidence fails to prove the product or WebMCP workflow.

one_line: Lets agents inspect tracks and create racing-line layouts on a map-based editor.
what_it_does: Edits braking, acceleration, and transition points on satellite maps, with 3D viewing, local persistence, undo, and save/load.
leverage_rationale: Racing-line edits require ordered, constrained geometry and shared editor state; structured tools reduce agent guessing versus UI driving, though humans could still perform the same edits manually.
leverage_evidence: About text says agents read circuit/reference/guidance and create missing layouts directly in the editor.
Tools expose inspection, point editing, undo, save/load.
Submitted frame sheet references a racing-line demo, while screenshot evidence is promotional and partial.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a focused editor with persistence, 3D view, tests, and a concrete missing-layout demo, but visible evidence is mainly a paused promotional frame rather than an end-to-end trace.
execution_evidence: Demo alive and three gallery images reported.
About text specifies Vite/React, IndexedDB, exports, Vitest and Playwright.
Frame-sheet description visibly presents an AI-drawn racing line on a track.
impact_rationale: Karting drivers and coaches can use racing-line visualization to learn unfamiliar tracks; the tool addresses a specific preparation and training need.
impact_evidence: Narrative identifies karting preparation and studying unfamiliar tracks.
Product supports braking, apex, and acceleration-zone representation.
creativity_rationale: Agent-authored, geometry-sensitive racing layouts are a memorable and unusual use of WebMCP, pursued with domain-specific constraints.
creativity_evidence: Concept combines satellite maps, racing-line semantics, and agent editing.
The six-year-old editor is separated and rebuilt as a standalone WebMCP app for the challenge.
usability_note: Domain-specific points and visible controls suggest a usable editor; agent correction and validation are not fully shown.
red_flags: Packet says open-source but FACTS report no public repo.
Promotional frame does not establish the full edit/save/validate sequence.
standouts: Distinctive niche use case.
Structured context addresses point ordering and drivable-surface constraints.
advance_reason: Original domain application with credible structured-editing leverage and visible generated racing-line result.

one_line: Turns natural-language street plans into editable 3D urban scenes via agent-operated WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Composes street segments, geolocates them, uses elevation/3D map context, and provides snapshots and machine-readable scene context for iterative design.
leverage_rationale: The agent composes many interdependent spatial edits while sharing live 3D scene state and camera/context metadata; replicating this comparably through generic UI driving would be substantially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Description claims 26 WebMCP tools for segment composition, geolocation, context, and snapshots.
About text describes shared scene state and getGeoContext bridge with bearing/endpoints.
Visible demo frame shows natural-language request, 3D street scene, and completed tool/activity rows.
execution_rationale: A coherent professional editor, agent chat, tool activity, and concrete street scene are visibly aligned; the packet does not fully prove persistence/export and every claimed tool.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repo are reported.
Video frame visibly shows BRT request, 3D street scene with bus, and tool activity panel.
Narrative describes presets, geolocation, elevation, plan-view snapshot, and self-correction.
impact_rationale: Planners, advocates, students, and communities can rapidly visualize safer street alternatives in real locations for discussion and decision-making; the fit is direct and credible.
impact_evidence: About text names planners, advocates, and students as existing users.
Use case explicitly targets designs brought to city-council meetings.
Visible result is an understandable 3D street/BRT visualization.
creativity_rationale: Natural-language agent composition of real-world, elevation-aware 3D street designs with self-observation is ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Combines conversational planning, geospatial anchoring, 3D Tiles context, and agent snapshots.
Segment presets preserve meaningful road semantics such as bus lanes and markings.
usability_note: The chat-plus-editor layout and tool activity make the collaborative workflow legible; density and full editing flow are not completely shown.
red_flags: Project is explicitly based on an existing open-source tool, so challenge-new scope is unclear though packet describes substantial WebMCP work.
Exact tool names/parameters are too small in still evidence.
standouts: Strongest shared-state WebMCP use in the packet.

Bounded unsent drafting avoids high-risk automatic outreach.

standouts: Strong human-agent co-design interaction.

one_line: Analyzes large sensitive files locally while exposing only safe aggregates to an agent.
what_it_does: Classifies columns, compiles bounded aggregate analysis, blocks row-level disclosure, revokes network access, and provides a disclosure receipt.
leverage_rationale: The privacy guarantee depends on in-page structured tools over data the agent cannot address; removing WebMCP removes the product rather than merely degrading convenience, and generic UI driving cannot safely reproduce the boundary.
leverage_evidence: Narrative explicitly says the project stops existing without WebMCP.
Eight tools omit run_sql and compile bounded forms instead.
Transcript claims zero raw rows returned, legal alternatives on refusal, and network revocation against five exfiltration paths.
execution_rationale: The packet provides unusually detailed transcript evidence of large-file processing, refusal/recovery behavior, disclosure accounting, and adversarial network checks, with a coherent visible interface; some claims remain self-reported.
execution_evidence: 145-second transcript describes million-row analysis, tool withdrawal after sealing, refusal of maximum salary, and chart result.
About text reports 98.9 MB read, 2.2 KB released, zero raw rows.
Screenshot visibly shows file metadata, column classifications, agent workspace, and disclosure panel.
impact_rationale: Organizations needing analysis of salaries or other sensitive datasets can obtain useful aggregate insight without uploading or exposing individual records to an AI agent.
impact_evidence: Concrete employee-compensation example with million rows.
Workflow provides medians/cohort sizes and charts while refusing exact-person outputs.
Receipt is searchable/exportable according to the narrative.
creativity_rationale: A local, agent-directed analytical system whose core interaction is governed by dynamic disclosure policy and self-revoking network access is genuinely novel and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Column grading dynamically withdraws and rewrites tools when sensitivity changes.
Refusals supply privacy-preserving alternatives rather than dead ends.
Adversarial exfiltration testing and literal agent-receipt search make the guarantee inspectable.
usability_note: The file panel, natural-language prompt, and disclosure accounting form a clear workflow; policy edge cases may require expertise.
red_flags: Privacy and performance claims are primarily submission-controlled evidence rather than independent audit.
Column grading is heuristic and can be wrong, though the packet explicitly discloses that limitation.
standouts: Strongest WebMCP indispensability in the packet.
Concrete zero-row disclosure story with visible refusal and recovery behavior.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP leverage, exceptional evidence quality, clear high-value use case, and unusually original safety architecture.
